description: The bar chart illustrates the performance of five different model configurations—Single-task_baseline, Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout, Unsupervised_SimCSE, Supervised_SimCSE, and 2-Tier SimCSE—across three evaluation metrics: Sentiment Accuracy (light yellow), STS Correlation (light pink), and Paraphrase Accuracy (light blue), as reported in the paper “2-Tier SimCSE: Elevating BERT for Robust Sentence Embeddings.” The vertical axis represents “Accuracy / Correlation,” ranging from 0 to 0.8 with tick marks at 0.2 intervals. Each model configuration is represented by a group of three adjacent bars, with the legend indicating the color coding for each metric. The 2-Tier SimCSE model achieves the highest STS Correlation (~0.81) and Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.78), while its Sentiment Accuracy (~0.49) is comparable to Supervised_SimCSE (~0.48) and slightly lower than Unsupervised_SimCSE (~0.52). The Single-task_baseline shows the lowest STS Correlation (~0.50) and moderate Paraphrase Accuracy (~0.79). Across all models, Paraphrase Accuracy remains consistently high (between ~0.77 and 0.80), while Sentiment Accuracy is generally lower (between ~0.48 and 0.53), and STS Correlation varies more widely, from ~0.50 to ~0.81. The chart visually emphasizes the performance gains of 2-Tier SimCSE, particularly in STS Correlation, relative to other SimCSE variants and baseline models.
